question: Does a multipath-trained per-channel E improve the per-bin phase readout over untrained E and masked reconstruction?
architecture: hybrid_small from experiments/encoder_phase_pilot/benchmark.py (C=16, F=43, T_e=15); proxy for E-S, not full E-M

objectives.recon: masked reconstruction of observed X; decoder Conv2d(C,2,1) + bilinear to T=29; MSE on masked TF
objectives.jepa: online E sees masked X; EMA teacher E(X_full); 3xConv2d predictor; MSE on masked TF to LayerNorm(sg(E_EMA(X_full))); EMA 0.996

mask.type: random 4x4 TF blocks, 30% of tokens, per sample
mask.input: nearest-upsample mask to T=29; masked Re/Im coefficients set to zero

data.train: 4095 sources x 8 channels, mp_cal, SNR groups 0/5/10 dB
data.val: 510 sources x 8 channels, mp_cal, SNR groups 0/5/10 dB
data.eval: 256 sources x 8 channels, mp_cal 10 and 0 dB

training.anti_collapse: EMA + stop-grad + VICReg-style variance term weight 0.01

evaluation.readout: per-bin cross-product ridge to [cos(phi), sin(phi)] of geometric direct path; fit on 8103, eval on 8102; 28 pairs; grid tau [-130,130] us

decision_rule.jepa_benefit: jepa >=20% better than untrained and recon on mp_cal 10 dB for >=2/3 seeds
decision_rule.recon_benefit_only: recon beats untrained but jepa does not; representation learning may help, JEPA mechanism not supported
decision_rule.no_benefit: neither beats untrained; negative result; pivot to benchmark/negative-result contribution
decision_rule.raw_reference: raw phase-slope remains the physical reference; E should approach <=3x raw

checks: train/val/readout/eval/test splits disjoint; fit/eval environments disjoint
mask canary: changing masked input does not change online output
untrained mp_cal baseline reproduces hard-regime 2.3-3.0 deg
git status clean and validator PASS
limits: simplified static multipath; one channel per training window; no Fusion
hybrid_small is a proxy, not E-M; 3 seeds are repeated trainings
CPU-generated data, GPU training, float32; dev/probe only
per-bin linear readout may be capacity-limited
diagnostic only; not an E gate or field result
